summary: The dedicated country dossier found no region-specific incident, enforcement pattern or ordinance for Sonora: it is not among the six states refusing any legal gender-recognition procedure, absent from the state-by-state lethality rankings, and outside the states where armed-group control was documented as an amplifier of risk to gender-nonconforming people. The national framework applies without a recorded regional deviation.

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time; the underlying source is a Human Rights Watch country overview (31 March 2025) on transgender rights progress and challenges in Mexico, headlining that 22 of the country's 32 states had legislated a legal gender-recognition procedure by that date and naming six whose legislatures had enacted none.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time; the underlying source is the Human Rights Watch report 'I Just Want to Contribute to Society' (6 March 2024) on the need for legal gender recognition in Tabasco, co-produced with the Centro Comunitario para la Inclusión, documenting that the absence of any recognition procedure leaves trans people exposed to police and institutional mistreatment.

The Guardian (24 July 2024): Mexico City's legislature approved the 'Paola Buenrostro law' making transfeminicide a distinct criminal offence, named for a trans woman murdered in 2016 whose killing remains unpunished; the report covers the vote and celebrants outside the congress building.
